finding.cause: The APP provider firewall has outbound default Drop and no UDP/123 allow rule, so systemd-timesyncd cannot reach ntp.ubuntu.com. The host firewall is inactive and is not the blocker.

liveApp.observedBehavior: Repeated timeouts to every resolved IPv4 and IPv6 Ubuntu NTP address for multiple days

evidence.establishes: APP firewall 224154258 is attached to APP, outbound default is Drop, and its four outbound rules allow only FIPS UDP/32121, provider DNS UDP/TCP 53, and TCP/443; UDP/123 is absent
The later validator firewall change preserved APP's enabled firewall with the same three inbound and four outbound rules
All MVP services are running without restarts, APP remains unsynchronized, and the last measured APP clock was 1.250 seconds behind the validator median

providerConstraint.cloudFirewallDestinations: IP addresses or CIDR ranges; hostnames are not accepted
providerConstraint.reasonNotToPinCurrentAddresses: ntp.ubuntu.com is a pool name and its resolved addresses can change; fixed /32 rules would be narrower but not durable

preconditions: Fresh provider readback shows firewall 224154258 remains enabled and attached only to APP interface 1112585
Outbound default remains Drop and the existing four outbound rules exactly match accepted evidence
APP remains NTPSynchronized=no and systemd-timesyncd remains active
APP has no in-progress auction or admission session
preserve: All existing inbound and outbound rules
All host firewall and systemd-timesyncd configuration
All auction, Comet, FROST, mint, HTTPS and application services
recommendedMutation.immediateConvergence: After provider save and exact readback, restart only systemd-timesyncd once so it sends a fresh request instead of waiting for its current backoff interval
forbidden: No manual date or RTC step
No NTP server installation on validators

provider: Exact post-save readback contains one new UDP/123 IPv4 outbound rule and no other delta
Firewall remains enabled and attached only to APP interface 1112585
time: systemd-timesyncd reports a valid NTP message and a positive packet count
Three bounded samples place APP within 0.500 seconds of the synchronized V1-V4 median
No backward or repeated correction is attempted
deployment: All previously active APP and V1-V4 services remain active-running
NRestarts remains zero for auction services
Authority returns two advancing ready samples after the time correction
acceptance.failurePolicy: Stop without broadening destinations, changing defaults, restarting application services, or retrying. Preserve provider and host readbacks for diagnosis. Any rollback or alternate server selection requires a separate decision.

security.benefit: Restores durable clock synchronization while preserving default-deny egress and limiting the new capability to the standard NTP destination port over IPv4.
risks: A compromised APP host could send UDP traffic to destination port 123 on arbitrary IPv4 addresses; the provider firewall remains stateful and unsolicited inbound traffic remains blocked.
NTP itself is not cryptographically authenticated; trust remains the operating system's Ubuntu pool configuration and DNS resolution.

The first successful synchronization may move APP's clock forward by approximately 1.25 seconds, changing application timestamps and invalidating in-flight readiness or admission windows. Perform it before real users begin an auction.
security.whyThisScope: The provider firewall cannot express an ntp.ubuntu.com hostname destination. Allowing all IPv4 destinations on only UDP/123 is the smallest configuration-only rule that remains functional when the pool rotates addresses; changing the global outbound default would be materially broader.

approvalScope: Add one outbound ACCEPT UDP/123 rule to 0.0.0.0/0 on APP firewall 224154258 while preserving all defaults and current rules, then restart only systemd-timesyncd once and perform the listed read-only verification.
